newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu denies peace pace stops investors.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu denies peace pace stops investors.

text.p: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Thursday investors were drawn to Israel without regard for the slow pace of peace moves.

"It's become clear that the investors don't make the connection to the political issue. It's become clear that the investors invest despite what's being said," he told reporters in Tel Aviv, rejecting charges his right-wing peace policies would deter foreign investment.
"Certainly there is a direct link, or an indirect link, but apparently it's not the dominant one," Netanyahu said.
Since taking office in June, the Israeli leader has angered Arabs by failing to implement a troop redeployment in the West Bank town of Hebron and by pledging to expand Jewish settlements.

Koor Industries Ltd, Israel's biggest conglomerate, said on Wednesday that a deteriorating economy and doubts about peacemaking contributed to an almost 10 percent decline in the concern's net profit in the third quarter.
Equity analysts who follow Koor expressed scepticism, saying most of the conglomerate's problems could be traced to subsidiaries in cement and electronics.
